subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-supported by default, or should recurring `deleteAfterRun` be treated as a one-shot-only contract?
rationale: This PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96045 encode opposite product contracts, and the safest code repair depends on which lifecycle rule maintainers want.

options.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Land this direction only after it handles both fresh creates and already-persisted omitted isolated recurring jobs, then pause or close the strict-rejection path.

options.title: Reject recurring delete-after-run
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation path after its Gateway/UI compatibility blockers are fixed.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Land this PR as-is and document that existing omitted jobs require operator action or a separate migration, accepting the remaining upgrade gap.

recommendation.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Land this direction only after it handles both fresh creates and already-persisted omitted isolated recurring jobs, then pause or close the strict-rejection path.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits at the cron normalization and migration boundary where recent path history points most strongly to steipete.
